title: Business operations
description: Review how recurring work moves between teams and whether the proposed change improves service without shifting delays or rework elsewhere.
expertises: Measurement and rollout of process changes
questions: What event starts the work, what counts as finished, and who accepts the result?
Where do cases wait, get sent back or require manual handling?
How does the team handle a demand spike, an absent owner or a case that doesn't fit the normal process?

sources.title: Lean Enterprise Institute, Value Stream Mapping

specialists.title: Process and handoffs
specialists.focus: Trace a typical request and an exception through the real handoffs, including what each team needs before it can act.
checks: A normal request and an exception are traced through every handoff.
Each handoff states what the next team needs before it can act.

specialists.title: Capacity and queues
specialists.focus: Locate the step where incoming work exceeds completion capacity and compare the effect of changing intake, batch size or staffing.
checks: Arrival and completion rates are measured at the step where work piles up.
Changes to intake, batch size or staffing are compared on the same measure.

specialists.title: Service quality and controls
specialists.focus: Check which reviews prevent incomplete or incorrect work and define who handles exceptions when those checks fail.
checks: Checks that prevent incorrect work are placed before the costly step.
Exceptions have an owner and a resolution time.

specialists.title: Process change lead
specialists.focus: Plan how the people who run the process learn the new steps, when the old way stops and how the change is measured after rollout.
checks: People who run the process are trained before the old way stops.
The date the old process stops and the measure of adoption are set.

evidence: Review the current process map and operating procedure with the people who perform the steps. Check the actual entry, exit and handoff criteria.
Inspect authorized aggregate arrival volume, queue age, completion time and rework over a representative period. Identify any groups missing from the data.
Use redacted examples of routine and exceptional cases to check how the receiving team handles missing inputs and who takes responsibility when work stalls.
Training, updated procedure and rollout date for the people who perform the changed steps.
challenge: Check whether faster processing in one team increases waiting, errors or manual work in the next team.
Walk through a demand spike and an exception with the owners. Identify where the proposed process needs escalation or a fallback.
Question any proposed automation that assumes clean input or removes a review without an equivalent check.
What happens to cases already in progress when the new process starts?
decision_criteria: Prefer the change that addresses the observed constraint and improves end-to-end completion without increasing rework or harming the agreed service target.
Assign one owner for each handoff and exception that changes. Describe what evidence the receiving team uses to accept the work.
Define a pilot with a representative set of cases, a review date and the result that would trigger returning to the current process.
Ask for a cut-over plan when cases in flight would follow two processes at once.
